paper.title: Ghostwriters of the Marketplace: A Corpus of Machine-Generated Reviews for Google Services and Businesses

collection.dataset_name: Ghostwriters of the Marketplace dataset (main and external AI-generated Google reviews)
collection_methods: Rehydration or extension of an existing dataset
collection.scale_description_verbatim: Our main dataset contains 78,724 AI-generated texts, distributed over texts generated by MULTI-STYLE, MULTI-TURN, and PARAPHRASED.

tasks_verbatim: determining whether a given review text was originally written by a human or was generated or faked by an AI model

ethics.anonymization_details: User information was not used in any way in this work. Only the AI-generated texts are published. The ReviewID consists of a combination of the gmap_id, user_id and a random number.

evidence.availability_quote: The dataset is assigned a persistent identifier (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18162470) and is registered in Zenodo, to ensure easy discovery by researchers and automated systems.
evidence.scale_quote: Our main dataset contains 78,724 AI-generated texts, distributed over texts generated by MULTI-STYLE, MULTI-TURN, and PARAPHRASED. Our external dataset, created for testing the generalizability of the detectors on unseen LLMs, contains overall 20,412 texts.
evidence.annotation_quote: This selection strategies resulted in 90,000 human written product reviews. We summarized each human written review into one or two sentences using GPT-4.1 and LLaMA-3.2-3b-instruct. The prompt used to generate each text is saved, together with the LLM used for generation, rate, and tone in the dataset.
evidence.ethics_quote: We did not use any personal information. If personal information is found in the dataset, that was not our intention. The dataset is shared for research purposes only. Still, the licence enables lawful reuse and citation.
evidence.license_quote: The dataset is shared for research purposes only. We choose this publication method as the Google Local Review dataset, on which our dataset is based on, was also published for research purposes only.
evidence.ambiguity_notes: The dataset is released on Zenodo under a research-only licence, which is not a standard open licence; it is coded as 'Custom terms or data use agreement' with the verbatim phrase 'research purposes only'. The 'supported_tasks' field includes 'Multimodal understanding' as a placeholder because the main task (AI-generated text detection) is a form of content classification not explicitly listed in the enum; 'Misinformation or claim detection' is used as the closest available enum value. The paper's license is 'research purposes only', which is more restrictive than a standard open licence, so it is coded as a custom terms.
